provenance.title: Adult sickle-cell disease — crisis recognition, hydroxyurea and transfusion referral
provenance.primarySource: WHO Sickle-cell disease: a handbook for community health workers and their supervisors; NHS Sickle Cell Society crisis management principles; Zimbabwe haemoglobinopathy care guidance (published summaries)
provenance.why: Adults with sickle-cell disease die from unrecognised acute chest syndrome, sepsis during vaso-occlusive crisis, and stroke — not from the pain episode itself. Hydroxyurea reduces crisis frequency but is under-used. Transfusion is a Madi-owned capability; this pack prompts referral without building a transfusion system of record.

sourceVerification.note: No WHO DAK for adult sickle-cell crisis management is vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against published WHO sickle-cell handbook and standard crisis-recognition criteria; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until MOHCC ratifies national thresholds. Transfusion referral points to Madi as the governed blood/transfusion rail — no transfusion SoR is created here.

rules.name: Vaso-occlusive crisis — treat pain promptly and investigate triggers
rules.message: Vaso-occlusive crisis — treat pain promptly and look for a precipitant.
rules.explanation: Bone and soft-tissue pain in a person with sickle-cell disease is a vaso-occlusive crisis until proven otherwise. Untreated pain prolongs admission; missed infection, dehydration or hypoxia turns a manageable crisis into acute chest syndrome.
rules.requiredAction: Start analgesia per protocol (including strong opioids if required), give IV fluids if dehydrated, check temperature and oxygen saturation, and screen for infection. Reassess within one hour of initial analgesia.
sourceRefs: Sickle-cell crisis management — analgesia and triggers

adaptation.whoStatement: Vaso-occlusive pain should be treated promptly with effective analgesia.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; analgesia ladder is a national protocol decision.

testCases.name: SCD with VOC pain — recognition fires
SCD without pain — does not fire

rules.name: Acute chest syndrome — emergency oxygen and exchange transfusion consideration
rules.message: Acute chest syndrome — medical emergency; oxygen, antibiotics and urgent specialist care.
rules.explanation: Acute chest syndrome — new pulmonary infiltrate with fever, cough, chest pain or hypoxia in sickle-cell disease — is the leading cause of death in adults. It overlaps with pneumonia and fat embolism and progresses within hours.
rules.requiredAction: Give supplemental oxygen to target saturation per protocol, start broad-spectrum antibiotics and incentive spirometry if tolerated, and arrange urgent haematology / high-dependency care. Consider exchange transfusion via Madi referral where national protocol indicates.
sourceRefs: WHO sickle-cell handbook — acute chest syndrome

adaptation.whoStatement: Acute chest syndrome requires prompt treatment including oxygen and antibiotics.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Exchange transfusion referral routed to Madi — transfusion execution is not owned by this pack.
adaptation.rationale: Adds explicit Madi referral language without building transfusion SoR.

testCases.name: SCD with acute chest — emergency fires
SCD without acute chest — does not fire

rules.name: Fever in sickle-cell disease — treat as sepsis until proven otherwise
rules.message: Fever in sickle-cell disease — assume serious bacterial infection until excluded.
rules.explanation: Functional asplenia and bone infarction make bacteraemia and osteomyelitis common and rapidly fatal in sickle-cell disease. A febrile patient needs blood cultures, prompt antibiotics and admission — not outpatient analgesia alone.
rules.requiredAction: Take blood cultures, start empiric parenteral antibiotics per local sepsis protocol, and admit for monitoring. Do not discharge on oral antibiotics alone without a clear source and improvement.
sourceRefs: Sepsis in sickle-cell disease — functional asplenia

adaptation.whoStatement: Fever in sickle-cell disease should be treated as potentially life-threatening infection.

testCases.name: SCD with fever — sepsis screen fires

rules.name: Recurrent crises — discuss hydroxyurea for frequency reduction
rules.message: Three or more vaso-occlusive crises in 12 months — discuss hydroxyurea.
rules.explanation: Hydroxyurea raises fetal haemoglobin, reduces crisis frequency and may protect against acute chest syndrome. It is under-prescribed in African adult cohorts despite strong evidence. The threshold here is a review prompt, not an automatic start — cytopenias and pregnancy must be excluded first.
rules.requiredAction: Discuss hydroxyurea with the patient: baseline FBC and renal function, contraception in women of childbearing potential, and haematology follow-up. Document shared decision and monitoring plan.
sourceRefs: Hydroxyurea for sickle-cell disease — evidence summary

adaptation.whoStatement: Hydroxyurea is recommended for patients with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Three crises in 12 months used as the review threshold pending national ratification.
adaptation.rationale: Uses three VOC episodes in 12 months as a national review threshold pending MOHCC ratification of the hydroxyurea start criterion.

testCases.name: three crises in 12 months — hydroxyurea prompt fires
episode count not supplied — must not fire

rules.name: Severe anaemia or stroke — refer to Madi for transfusion / exchange
rules.message: Transfusion indicated — refer through Madi; this pack does not execute transfusion.
rules.explanation: Symptomatic severe anaemia, acute stroke, or refractory acute chest syndrome may require simple or exchange transfusion. Blood product issue, cross-match and transfusion documentation are owned by Madi — the national transfusion rail — not by adult medicine or this content pack.
rules.requiredAction: Initiate Madi transfusion referral with indication, haemoglobin, and urgency. Continue supportive care while awaiting product. Do not attempt to record transfusion as complete in this workspace — execution belongs to Madi.

adaptation.whoStatement: Transfusion may be required for severe anaemia, stroke or acute chest syndrome in sickle-cell disease.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Referral routed to Madi; no transfusion SoR is built in CKP or adult medicine.
adaptation.rationale: Routes transfusion/exchange to Madi as the governed transfusion rail rather than creating a transfusion SoR in this pack.
